attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The signed or scale-sharp estimate of lambda_min(K_v^sing) for the actual regulated Yang-Mills endpoint box is still missing.
steps: Start from heat-kernel plaquette-sheet Wilson observables and expand each endpoint-local holonomy to fourth order in the smeared flux Phi_alpha,v.
Separate disconnected Wick contractions. Their contribution is a positive Gram square in the OS quotient and cannot decrease the corrected Schur-Feshbach null form.
Project the remaining four-flux cumulant to the singlet color channel. The fundamental traces give the factor (T_F/N)^2, and the two second-order insertions give the coefficient g^4/4.
Write each loop's endpoint contribution as p_i,v=sym(sigma_i,v otimes sigma_i,v). Bilinearity gives R_ij,v=(g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 <p_i,v,K_v^sing p_j,v> plus tail.
Apply the null vector only after the H,K Schur-Feshbach reduction. This replaces the finite matrix combination of R_ij by the single compressed vector p_xi,v=sum_i xi_i p_i,v.
Use the previously checked straight-incidence identity to kill the local C_A f f contact on non-endpoint portions; any surviving commutator term is pushed into endpoint/corner support.
Bound the compressed endpoint contribution below by the negative spectral radius Lambda_v^- times the incidence norm I_v=||p_xi,v||^2, then add the absolute endpoint tail bound.
Compare this negative allowance with the positive Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin M_G. Strict domination promotes the finite hairpin block; violation with a stable eigenvector demotes it.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The compression and inequality are valid finite-dimensional reductions, but the analysis has not proved a regulator-uniform bound on the irreducible connected four-flux endpoint cumulant or on E_tail.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint-box kappa_4 compression for the post-H,K Wilson collar term

assumptions: The heat-kernel regulator h_epsilon is gauge-covariant, reflection compatible, and removed only after the endpoint-box estimates are uniform in epsilon and lattice spacing.
The Wilson expansion is used only inside fixed endpoint boxes; the remainder is bounded uniformly by a local exponential moment for smeared plaquette fluxes.
Wick pairings of the four flux insertions have already been placed in the positive Gram term and are not counted inside K_v^sing.
The straight-segment C_A f f contact cancels under the previously identified null incidence identity, leaving only endpoint/corner support and the irreducible connected cumulant.
The endpoint boxes are disjoint at scale ell, and the outside contribution is collected in E_tail with a regulator-uniform bound.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated Wilson hairpin triple with endpoint boxes B_v(ell) and collar width delta before delta downarrow 0.
target object: corrected Schur-Feshbach null-channel endpoint contribution to the continuum OS quotient matrix after H,K are fixed.
controlled interface: regulated singlet connected four-flux cumulants K_v^sing and endpoint tails replace the abstract R_ij entries.

same-theory condition: Wilson loops, heat-kernel smearing, color trace normalization, and endpoint-box subtraction are locked before and after collar removal; no boundary counterterm or changed loop algebra is allowed.
Endpoint label alpha denotes an oriented plaquette-sheet germ incident at v, including its bivector n_alpha and Wilson-loop membership.
p_{i,v}=sym(sigma_{i,v} otimes sigma_{i,v}) is the pair-incidence vector for loop i at endpoint v, and p_{xi,v}=sum_i xi_i p_{i,v} for the Schur-Feshbach null vector xi.

equations.label: smeared endpoint flux
equations.valid_when: Valid when the reflected Wilson sheets are represented by heat-kernel smeared plaquette surfaces inside a fixed endpoint box.

equations.label: singlet connected four-flux endpoint matrix
equations.valid_when: Applies after Wick pairings are subtracted and only the irreducible connected four-flux cumulant remains.

equations.label: endpoint contribution to R
equations.valid_when: Requires the same-theory boundary OPE normalization for traced fundamental Wilson loops and fixed endpoint boxes.

equations.label: null-channel compression
equations.latex: \mathcal R_{\xi,v}^{(4,c)}=\frac{g^4}{4}\left(\frac{T_F}{N}\right)^2\langle p_{\xi,v},\mathcal K_v^{\rm sing}p_{\xi,v}\rangle+E_{\xi,v}^{\rm tail},\qquad p_{\xi,v}=\sum_i\xi_i p_{i,v}
equations.valid_when: Valid when the Schur-Feshbach null vector is applied after H passes PHP and the corrected K gate is isolated.

equations.label: negative-spectrum bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after diagonal normalization and after endpoint/corner tails have been separated from the local cumulant matrix.

equations.label: promotion inequality
equations.valid_when: Valid when M_G is the already computed positive Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin for this hairpin block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a regulator-stable endpoint eigenvector p with negative value large enough to violate the promotion inequality while the Wick-square and straight f f cancellations remain valid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma is the paper-handoff bridge from the symbolic R entries to a concrete Yang-Mills endpoint cumulant estimate with explicit color factor, regulator, cancellations, and sign condition.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the first reflected Wilson hairpin triple, after the Wick-square Gram part and the straight f f commutator contact are removed, the remaining post-H,K null-channel R contribution is a finite endpoint-box singlet four-flux cumulant plus a tail. A uniform negative-spectrum bound on this endpoint matrix is a valid promotion test, and a violating aligned negative eigenvector is a same-theory falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot only if endpoint orientation auditing shows the straight f f cancellation was false or if heat-kernel smearing changes the Wilson same-theory algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the finite hairpin block if the regulator-uniform bound (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 sum_v Lambda_v^- I_v plus tail is strictly below M_G.
control_decision.reason: The branch has reached the concrete post-H,K endpoint-box term; the next contribution is a signed computation or rigorous bound for K_v^sing, not another obstruction-ladder restatement.

dependency_updates.description: Need a regulator-uniform estimate or computation of lambda_min for the singlet connected four-flux endpoint matrix K_v^sing.
The bulk commutator contact cancels in the null channel; only endpoint/corner residues must be checked.
Disconnected Wick-square contractions enter as positive Gram terms and cannot be the post-H,K falsifier.
Need a uniform estimate for contributions outside endpoint boxes after the straight-contact cancellation.

falsifiers: A direct plaquette-source derivative computation gives lambda_min(K_v^sing)<0 with the aligned incidence norm large enough to violate the promotion inequality; this is the main finite endpoint falsifier.
The straight f f contact cancellation fails at corners because the endpoint orientation data do not satisfy the same null incidence identity as the straight shared segment.
The heat-kernel regulator produces a boundary counterterm or cusp renormalization not expressible through the locked Wilson-loop normalization, breaking the same-theory condition.
The endpoint tail is not small uniformly as epsilon and the lattice spacing are removed, so the finite endpoint-box reduction is not valid.
The connected four-flux cumulant has a reflection-plane contact term with indefinite sign that is not captured by the singlet endpoint matrix.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 246 compresses the remaining R problem to a finite endpoint spectral inequality. The actual Yang-Mills input is K_v^sing, the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet connected four-flux cumulant. Wick-square positivity and straight f f incidence cancellation remove the safe pieces; only negative endpoint spectrum and tails can defeat the positive Schur-Feshbach margin. The branch is not looping because it now has a computable regulator-level matrix, an incidence norm, and a valid promotion/falsifier inequality.
